 Order

This second appeal under Section 14-A (1 & 2) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been filed assailing the order dated 03.03.2023 passed by learned Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, District Chhatarpur (M.P.), whereby bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of appellant/accused has been dismissed.
2. Appellant has been arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.682/2022 dated 20.11.2022 registered at Police Station - Nawgoan, District Chhatarpur (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 376(2)(n), 294, 506 of IPC, Sections 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s), 3(1)(w)(i), 3(2)(va) and Section 3(2)(v) of Ramjee Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177255802/

sentences.text: Appellant is in detention since 26.12.2022.

3. Appellant's first bail application in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14-A of SC/ST act was disposed of as withdrawn and not pressed with liberty to revive the prayer for bail after evidence of prosecutrix before the trial Court or receipt of DNA report, whichever is earlier, vide order dated 01.05.2023 passed in CRA No.3747 of 2023.
4.
As per the prosecution story, on 20.11.2022, 32 years old prosecutrix lodged an F.I.R. alleging that she belongs to Scheduled Caste and used to perform dance program in orchestra.
On 19.11.2022 at about 10:00 am in the morning, applicant Ramjee Yadav made a call and hired her for a program for Rs.3,000/-.
At around 07:30 pm at Nawgaon Bus Stand, Ramjee Yadav met her on a motor-cylce and took her towards Garroli and thereafter, committed rape upon her in the forest.
When she tried to run away then again committed the same act with her.
After investigation charge-sheet has been filed.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that appellant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
It is submitted that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
She has turned hostile and has stated that as applicant had not paid remuneration to her, she had lodged false F.I.R.
After investigation, charge- sheet has been filed.
Therefore, it has been prayed that he may be released on bail.
6. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of bail to the appellant/accused.
7. I have gone through the prosecutrix's evidence recorded before the trial Court.

Having taken into consideration the all the facts & circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which appellant may be released on bail.
Consequently, this bail application in the form of criminal appeal under Section 14-A (1) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is allowed.

8. It is directed that appellant - Ramjee Yadav be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand o nly ) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
9.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE @shish Ramjee Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177255802/
